companion.title: Assessment of force control for surface finishing – an experimental comparison between Universal Robots UR10e and FerRobotics active contact flange
companion.locators: Sections 4–7, Figures 4, 7, 11, Table 2, appendix B. Authors describe ATI Delta SI-660-60 under the workpiece, TCP transformation, 800 µs ATI / 2 ms robot timing and five-run averages.

terms: Assessment of force control for surface finishing
prior_related_bibliography.reason: The journal work is historical. This fixed numerical-figure artifact and its repository identifiers were not in the prior retained evidence.

scope: Physical UR10e, ACF-K and iron reel on test surfaces or direct sensor contact. This is a force-control comparison on finishing surrogate paths. ATI fixture signal is an independent physical reference transformed to TCP using robot orientation, not an independent six-axis load history at the wrist. The ACF and UR are alternative controller configurations, not simultaneous robot-side force sensors. Original force/time arrays are not included in this fixed release; the individually exported vector figures and publisher numerical evaluation tables were verified.
measurement: All 67 individual single-controller force plots (23 ramp, 36 straight, 8 direct contact) have one blue measured Fz path and one red desired Fd. Read vector segment endpoints, match both axes to printed numeric ticks and PDF grid lines. Reconstruct N and s with linear interpolation and check for monotone paired timestamps and affine tick residual <0.03 axis units. Force values reported to 0.001 N purely for reproduction, not experimental precision (published normal-force resolution 0.25 N). Baseline from −0.5 to −0.1 s is on the author-aligned clock. Calculate contact-window samples for [0,4) s ramp/straight and [0,6) s direct, consistent with the author periods; boundary rounding can shift a single sample. Peak timing relative to the registered zero is not independent contact-onset latency.
tables: All 14 per-controller scenario/speed mean PDFs contain 68 condition rows. Extract numerical columns using their page positions, keeping a blank for undefined settling and identifying an explicit aborted trial condition. Link single-profile maximum error to the five-run averaged maximum error by (scenario, controller, speed, force, gain or ramp). Figures named _1_ represent plotted single runs; comparison, current and velocity figure renderings are not additional trials. The paper reports means across five repetitions; individual waveforms for all five cannot be recovered from this release.
results: Across 877,085 plotted vertices, all 67 individual curves matched one completed table condition. One of 68 conditions (UR ramp, 55 N, 0.25 m/s, gain 1) explicitly aborted on maximum position deviation; six completed conditions have no settling time in the published tables. For the direct-contact 100 N settings, four individual 0.25 m/s plots reach 929.930 to 1163.722 N versus the 0.1 m/s plots at 283.094 to 494.009 N. These are registered single-trace peaks, not the five-run averages. The pre-event Fz medians span −0.161 to 0.167 N, without an independent applied torque or unloaded wrist reference.
